# P31.11 (DEEPEN.7): human review decisions into camera-site clustering + duplicate-target lineage

Implements `docs/tickets/P31.11__review-decisions-into-clustering.md` (Round 9 Wave B,
manifest row 152). New **ADR-116** (the design's ADR-R9-HUMANER); **closes
D-P30.2b-3** (within-source duplicate layers), **advances — does not close —
D-P30.2b-1** (its closure leg is real human decisions clustering on hosted, a
Round-10 item); D-R6.1-EVAL untouched. Stacked on the P31.10 tip
`devin/p31-10-camera-site-review-surface` (PR #146).

The camera-site ER run now consumes the append-only `review_decision` history —
including **zero** decisions, which is the expected hosted state — without ever
waiting on a campaign.

## Summary

- **Human verdict folding (`resolution/camera_sites.py`, pure + deterministic).**
  `HumanItem` / `HumanVote` / `HumanVerdict` + `fold_human_verdicts`: every
  `review_decision` on `er_match:camera_site*` items (proposals,
  `camera_site_disputed:`, the new routed-back `camera_site_conflict:` family)
  folds to one verdict per *pair* — the most recently decided item governs, a
  timestamp tie between disagreeing items is itself a conflict. A pair with a
  human verdict takes the human outcome **before** any automatic edge:
  `accept` → `human_accept` same_as edge applied under the same hard
  constraints (`decided_by` = curator); `reject` → `human_reject` recorded as a
  hard `cannot_link` (the pair never clusters); `conflict` stays `proposed`
  (reason `human_conflict`) and is routed back under
  `er_match:camera_site_conflict:<a>:<b>` carrying the disagreeing history — a
  clean adjudication there supersedes next run. An accept that would violate a
  hard constraint (same-source without duplicate evidence, incompatible class,
  span/size) is recorded **`refused`** — never silently applied. P31.3
  `identity_duplicate` decisions stay with identity triage.
- **Duplicate-target lineage (closes D-P30.2b-3).** `infer_duplicate_targets`:
  one source's records group when row-identical (all projected fields +
  normalised ref + coordinate pair, with an identifying field so content-free
  stubs never qualify) or when their targets are proven byte-identical (shared
  `evidence_capture.content_digest` + same normalised ref). Members count as
  ONE effective record under constraint (a) — union-find, one-to-one neighbour
  counts and the `same_source_cluster` alert compare `(source, dup-root)`
  effective identities — and record tier-0 `0:duplicate_target_of` auto_write
  edges carrying the lineage proof. Genuinely distinct same-source devices at
  one point still never merge (test-pinned).
- **PG seam (`camera_sites_pg.py`).** `read_camera_records` now joins
  `entity_identifier` (`sig.connector.subject` → target) and
  `claim_evidence → evidence_capture` (`content_digest`s).
  `read_human_verdicts` reads `review_item`/`review_decision`. Materialization
  writes `relation_type`, `decided_by`, the verdict audit trail inside
  `match_evidence`, and conflict route-back items — all `INSERT … ON CONFLICT
  DO NOTHING`, append-only. `read_resolved_site_runs` returns
  `resolved_edges` = auto_write ∪ human_accept plus proposed/cannot_link/
  refused counts. Dry-run and materialize CLI paths both wire the verdicts in.
- **Sqitch `camera_site_human_decisions`** (new change, never an in-place
  edit): widens `camera_site_match.disposition` (+`human_accept`,
  `human_reject`, `refused`) and `relation_type` (+`cannot_link`) CHECKs;
  grants `sig_materialize` SELECT on `review_decision`. Revert **refuses
  loudly** if widened rows exist — human-decision history is never re-labelled.
- **Metric (`exports/spine_export.py`).** `resolved_sites` unions auto-write +
  human-accept edges; the population note splits `{auto_merges}` auto vs
  `{human_merges}` human-accepted merges, `{proposed}` still awaiting review,
  `{cannot_link}` rejects, `{refused}` constraint-refusals — none fabricated.
- **Run identity.** `run_key` digests the folded verdicts + the records' new
  lineage fields, so a new decision mints a new run; `decision_digest` carries
  relation/disposition/decided_by. `camera_site_run.summary.human_review`
  reports verdict counts, applied/refused edges, cannot-links, clusters
  carrying a human edge, and awaiting-review proposals.

## Verification

- `make check` — exit 0 (4,291 passed / 3 skipped; lint, format, mypy 258 files,
  verify-gen clean).
- `make test-db` — 280 passed on real PG18+PostGIS; new
  `tests/db/test_camera_site_human_decisions.py` (10 tests): accept clusters
  with curator attribution, reject → cannot_link never clusters, conflict stays
  proposed + conflict item enqueued, routed-back adjudication supersedes,
  refused constraint violations recorded-not-applied, duplicate-target merges
  on identical captures/rows, distinct same-source devices never merge,
  zero-decision == pre-wiring outcome, stable public ids, append-only privilege
  refusals.
- Pure suite `tests/resolution` — 422 passed (fold, precedence, refusal,
  duplicate-target, +0 re-run, summary counts).
- Export tests updated — human accepts counted, proposals disclosed.

Hosted (`sig-materialize` Cloud Run, digest-pinned images): camera-site
`review_decision` count measured **0** before the run (the only 3 hosted
decisions are P31.3 `identity_duplicate` rows, correctly ignored); sqitch
`camera_site_human_decisions` deployed `.. ok`. On the final image
`materialize-f9e548f652d2` (`sha256:102389ea…`): execution
`sig-materialize-g2qm6` wrote run `camsite:f03d71de…` — M **231,769** → N
**223,045**, 45,011 decisions (11,106 auto_write / 33,905 proposed),
`human_review` all-zero with 33,905 awaiting review; duplicate-target
measurement **26,129 groups / 57,257 records** (31,128 tier-0 edges: 4,960
applied, 26,168 proposed under `cluster_constraint:max_span`). Re-run
`sig-materialize-6tqtv` = **+0** (`inserted 0`, `skipped_existing 45,011`,
`run_record_inserted false`). Evidence:
`docs/build/reports/p31.11-hosted/camera_site_run.json`.

The hosted leg also surfaced a **pre-existing defect** (latent since P30.2b):
`_rules_digest` hashed `repr(rules)`, which leaks `PYTHONHASHSEED` ordering —
stable inputs minted new `run_key`s (three distinct 1.1.0 keys; explains the
two 1.0.0 keys too). Fixed in `f9e548f` by canonicalising
dataclasses/mappings/sets before hashing; regression-pinned. A crashed
execution's 4,000-row partial was also recovered append-only on hosted
(`rwkq6` skipped existing + inserted the remaining 41,011).
